description: A research study, trial, or project context under which biological samples and associated datasets are collected, grouped, and managed for specific research objectives.
A unique character string or persistent identifier that unambiguously distinguishes this study.
The official title, full name, or public label designating this study or research project.
A narrative summary outlining the scientific background, main objectives, and overall scope of the study.
A resolvable web address, digital object identifier (DOI) link, or persistent public repository URL pointing to the study documentation, trial registration, or associated online publication.
The primary medical, demographic, or genetic eligibility criteria required for a participant to be enrolled in this study.
The primary scientific leader, lead researcher, or designated contact person responsible for the design, execution, and integrity of the study.
An email address for the purpose of contacting the study contact person.

The methodological framework and operational protocol specification describing how subjects, biospecimens, and data are structured and collected (e.g. cohort, case-control, longitudinal, cross-sectional).
The date on which this study began.
The date on which all study protocols are finalized, participant follow-ups conclude, or the primary research objectives are fully met.
Reference to the study or studies in which this person participates.
Reference to the study for which this individual consent permits data and sample use.
Demographic, phenotypic, and baseline characteristics of an individual study participant or patient from whom biological materials and associated research data are collected.
A unique pseudonymised code or persistent subject identifier assigned to an individual within the study or biobank repository.
The gender or biological sex assigned to the individual at birth, typically documented in medical records or official birth certificates.
The sovereign country where the individual primarily resides at the time of study enrolment or sample collection.
The genetic or geographic ancestral background of an individual, evaluated using ancestry-informative genomic markers or population categories.
The country in which the individual was born.
The year in which the individual person was born.
The most recent vital or clinical follow-up status of the individual recorded by the biobank or registry (e.g. alive, deceased, lost to follow-up).
In the event of participant decease, the calculated age of the individual at the time of death, measured in completed years.
The primary healthcare facility, clinical centre, or biobank institution responsible for the medical management or enrolment of the individual.
Reference to the study or studies in which this person participates.
Reference to the person (i.e. subject) to whom this individual consent applies.
Reference to the person whom this clinical information is about.
Reference to the person from whom this material was collected.
Reference to the person whom this imaging study is about.
Specification and metadata of the informative leaflet and blank informed consent template version approved for a study or biobank collection.
A unique persistent identifier, DOI, or resolvable URL unambiguously identifying this specific consent template and leaflet pair.
The formal document title of the informed consent form template.
The authoritative biobank institution, hospital, or governance board that authored and issued this consent form.
The formal version number, release tag, or revision identifier of this consent form template.
Link to the specific approved template version in the Leaflet and consent form module used during signing.
Record of a signed informed consent given by an individual or legal guardian, specifying data and sample use permissions, restrictions, and validity periods.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular signed individual consent.
Reference to the person (i.e. subject) to whom this individual consent applies.
Link to the specific approved template version in the Leaflet and consent form module used during signing.
Reference to the study for which this individual consent permits data and sample use.
The healthcare facility, clinical ward, or biobank site where the informed consent was administered and obtained.
A date specification that designates when this individual consent form was signed.
The expiry date or termination date of the consent, such as upon participant withdrawal or completion of a time-limited study protocol.
An individual who is authorized under applicable State or local law to consent on behalf of a child or incapable person to general medical care including participation in clinical research.
The primary consented permission and intended scope governing the secondary research use of datasets and biological specimens.
Data use modifiers indicate additional conditions for use. For instance, a dataset is restricted to investigations into specific diseases or performed at specific geographical locations.
Indication of whether the participant has consented to be re-contacted by the biobank or clinical team for study updates, further sample donations, or actionable secondary health findings.
Clinical observations, diagnoses, disease staging, and longitudinal treatment responses recorded for a patient across specific disease encounters or study timepoints.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular clinical examination.
Reference to the person whom this clinical information is about.
Main clinical diagnosis coded using ICD-10, ORPHA, or SNOMED CT.
Age of the patient in years at the time of disease diagnosis.
Relative timepoint or clinical phase of this encounter relative to diagnosis or baseline (e.g. Baseline, Post-treatment, Relapse, Day 0, Month 3).
Broad categorisation of disease progression at the time of data or sample collection (e.g. Stage I-IV, Early/Advanced, Primary/Metastatic).

Causal gene(s) bearing a confirmed pathogenic or clinically significant variant associated with the patient's diagnosis or response to treatment (e.g. BRCA1, EGFR, KRAS). Do not list all tested panel genes here.
High-level classification of therapies applied to the patient (e.g. Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy, Immunotherapy, Surgery, Naive/Untreated).
The patients' response to the applied treatment regimen.
Reference to a diagnosis c.q. clinical examination of which this material may be a part of. There can be multiple diagnoses when a non-tumor material is reused as reference.
Reference to the specific clinical examination, diagnosis, or disease timepoint during which this imaging study was indicated or evaluated.

Primary biological material obtained directly from a donor or patient through a collection procedure (e.g. biopsy, surgery, blood draw), defining the original anatomical source, sampling timestamp, and pathological state.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular material.
Reference to the person from whom this material was collected.
Reference to a diagnosis c.q. clinical examination of which this material may be a part of. There can be multiple diagnoses when a non-tumor material is reused as reference.
The date that a sample was collected or obtained.
The broad biological nature of the collected substance prior to processing (e.g. whole blood, solid tissue, bone marrow, saliva, urine).
The specific organ, anatomical site, or bodily structure of the individual from which the biological material was procured.
The histological or pathological condition of the procured biological specimen or biofluid (e.g. malignant, benign, non-involved control, premalignant).

Identifies the parent biological Material entity from which this biospecimen directly or indirectly originates, either as a physical portion (aliquot) or as a derived fraction (e.g., extracted DNA, serum, tissue section).

A specific physical unit, aliquot, or processed preparation derived from primary material (e.g. FFPE block, frozen tissue section, biofluid aliquot) managed in biobank storage under defined preservation and fixation conditions.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular biospecimen.

Identifies the parent biological Material entity from which this biospecimen directly or indirectly originates, either as a physical portion (aliquot) or as a derived fraction (e.g., extracted DNA, serum, tissue section).

The specific physical form, fraction, or analyte derived from the parent material (e.g., extracted genomic DNA, total RNA, serum, cell lysate, or FFPE section) prepared for downstream analysis or sequencing.
The percentage of tumor cells compared to total cells present in this material.
The total count or number of available physical units, aliquots, blocks, or slides representing this specific biospecimen instance.
The environmental temperature and preservation parameter under which the biospecimen is maintained in the repository.
The organization or facility that owns, manages, and physically stores this biospecimen or slide, maintaining custody and responsibility for its storage conditions and associated data.
The current operational or inventory status indicating whether the biospecimen is available for research, reserved, depleted, or destroyed.
The name of the compound that preserves tissues and cells for microscopic study.
A material that infiltrates and supports a specimen and preserves its shape and structure for sectioning and microscopy.
Reference to the biospecimen (e.g. FFPE block, slide) that was the physical input to this slide preparation assay.
Reference to the source biospecimen from which this sample was prepared.

A diagnostic, clinical, or research imaging procedure comprising one or more imaging series (e.g. radiological scans such as CT/MRI or digital pathology whole slide images) acquired for a subject within a common clinical or study context.
The user- or equipment-generated identifier of an instance of a study entity.
Reference to the person whom this imaging study is about.
Reference to the specific clinical examination, diagnosis, or disease timepoint during which this imaging study was indicated or evaluated.
The date on which a study began.

An imaging procedure as defined by SNOMED CT, representing a specific diagnostic or acquisition procedure (e.g., 'CT of breast', 'MRI of head', or 'Whole Slide Imaging'), rather than the general modality or technique alone. The general modality or technique (e.g., 'CT', 'MR', 'SM') is captured separately in the 'Imaging modality' field.

The clinical or research rationale for performing the imaging procedure. This field captures why the procedure was indicated for the patient, such as screening, diagnosis, treatment planning, or research purposes. It should express the intent or medical reason, not the technical details of the procedure itself.
The total number of image series contained within this imaging study.
The total number of individual image instances or frames comprising this imaging study.
The organisation or institution responsible for performing the imaging study.
Reference to the subsequent imaging study or digital whole-slide scanning event for which this prepared slide serves as the direct physical input.
Parent study context.
Parent study context.
Parent study context.
Parent study context.
Parent study context.
Parent study context.
Parent study context.

A laboratory protocol for preparing, sectioning, and staining biological specimens on glass slides (e.g. histological, special staining, or immunohistochemistry assays) prior to whole slide imaging or microscopic evaluation.
An assay identifier is an identifier that identifies some assay (analysis).

The specific type of laboratory test or analytical procedure performed on a bio-specimen mounted on a glass slide. It defines the staining or labeling technique applied to the specimen to reveal specific structural, molecular, or cellular features.
Reference to the biospecimen (e.g. FFPE block, slide) that was the physical input to this slide preparation assay.
Reference to the subsequent imaging study or digital whole-slide scanning event for which this prepared slide serves as the direct physical input.

A classification of the type of biomolecule or biological component that the assay targets, labels, or detects. It characterizes whether the biomarker is, for example, a protein, nucleic acid, carbohydrate, lipid, or inorganic substance.
A measurement of the thickness of a sectioned slice (of tissue or mineral or other substance), expressed in micrometers (µm).
The subcellular or structural location within a tissue or cell where the biomarker is expressed or detected.
Identification of the specific type of pathogen among the listed categories e.g. 'Virus','Viroid','Bacterium'...
The neutral or synthetic colored substance used for staining specific tissues or cellular components.
The counter-labeling technique used to highlight specific cellular or tissue structures, serving as a complementary method to the primary labeling for analysis
The vendor-stated name of an antibody used to detect and visualize the presence of an antigen.
An assay identifier is an identifier that identifies some assay (analysis).
The pre-analytical laboratory procedure used to extract, isolate, and prepare nucleic acids into sequencing libraries, including target enrichment, molecular barcoding, and library quality control.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular sample preparation.
Reference to the source biospecimen from which this sample was prepared.
Amount of input material in nanogram (ng).

Pre-filled, ready-to-use reagent cartridges intented to improve chemistry, cluster density and read length as well as improve quality (Q) scores for this sample. Reagent components are encoded to interact with the sequencing system to validate compatibility with user-defined applications.

Indicates whether a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was used to prepare this sample. PCR is a method for amplifying a DNA base sequence using multiple rounds of heat denaturation of the DNA and annealing of oligonucleotide primers complementary to flanking regions in the presence of a heat-stable polymerase.

Indicates which target enrichment kit was used to prepare this sample. Target enrichment is a pre-sequencing DNA preparation step where DNA sequences are either directly amplified (amplicon or multiplex PCR-based) or captured (hybrid capture-based) in order to only focus on specific regions of a genome or DNA sample.
List of genes where the entire coding sequence (all exons) was targeted and sequenced.
List of genes where only specific regions or hotspots (selected exons/codons) were targeted and sequenced.
Indicates whether any unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are present. An UMI barcode is a short nucleotide sequence that is used to identify reads originating from an individual mRNA molecule.

In paired-end sequencing, the DNA between the adapter sequences is the insert. The length of this sequence is known as the insert size, not to be confused with the inner distance between reads. So, fragment length equals read adapter length (2x) plus insert size, and insert size equals read lenght (2x) plus inner distance.
The number of nucleotides intended to be ordered from each side of a nucleic acid fragment obtained after the completion of a sequencing process.
Reference to the prepared sample, i.e. the source that was sequenced.
Technical execution and instrument run parameters of a high-throughput sequencing assay, including sequencer platform, read metrics, coverage depth, and sequencing quality control statistics.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular nucleic acid sequencing assay.
Reference to the prepared sample, i.e. the source that was sequenced.
Date on which this sequencing assay was performed.
The used sequencing platform (i.e. brand, name of a company that produces sequencer equipment).
The used product name and model number of a manufacturer's genomic (dna) sequencer.
Method used to determine the order of bases in a nucleic acid sequence.
The median number of times a particular locus (site, nucleotide, amplicon, region) was sequenced.
The number of nucleotides successfully ordered from each side of a nucleic acid fragment obtained after the completion of a sequencing process.

In paired-end sequencing, the DNA between the adapter sequences is the insert. The length of this sequence is known as the insert size, not to be confused with the inner distance between reads. So, fragment length equals read adapter length (2x) plus insert size, and insert size equals read lenght (2x) plus inner distance.
Percentage of reads with a Phred quality score over 30, which indicates less than a 1/1000 chance that the base was called incorrectly.
Percentage of the target sequence on which 20 or more unique reads were successfully mapped.

Other NGS quality control metrics, including but not limited to (i) sequencer metrics such as yield, error rate, density (K/mm2), cluster PF (%) and phas/prephas (%), (ii) alignment metrics such as QM insert size, GC content, QM duplicated reads (%), QM error rate, uniformity/evenness of coverage and maternal cell contamination, and (iii) variant call metrics such as number of SNVs/CNVs/SVs called, number of missense/nonsense variants, common variants (%), unique variants (%), gender match and trio inheritance check.
Reference to the sequencing that was performed, i.e. the source on which this analysis was based.

Computational and bioinformatic processing workflows applied to primary sequencing data, including reference genome alignment, variant calling algorithms, standard pipeline guidelines, and stored output file formats.
A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular analysis.
Reference to the sequencing that was performed, i.e. the source on which this analysis was based.
Which data file formats (i.e. defined ways or layouts of representing and structuring data in a computer file, blob, string, message, or elsewhere) are stored and potentially available.
Any used problem-solving procedures implemented in software to be executed by a computer.
The specific build of the human genome used as reference for sequence alignment and variant calling.

A human-readable collection of information about about how a scientific experiment or analysis was carried out that results in a specific set of data or results used for further analysis or to test a specific hypothesis.
Common metadata and technical characteristics for a coherent series of biomedical image instances acquired using a single equipment, coordinate frame, and imaging modality within an imaging study.
A unique identifier for series of images.
Parent study context.
The total number of discrete image instances, slices, or frames contained within this imaging series.
Any technology or method that aids in the visualization of any biological process, cell, tissue or organ for use in screening, diagnosis, surgical procedures or therapy.
The date on which a series began.
The specific anatomical region, body part, or organ targeted by this imaging series.
The side of the body or paired organ being examined (e.g. Left, Right, Bilateral, Unilateral).
A device for producing a representation or picture, usually of a part of the body, to aid in diagnosis and evaluation.
A person, enterprise, or entity that produces imaging device.
A form or variant of software; one of a sequence of copies of a software program, each incorporating new modifications.
The photometric interpretation of pixel data that defines the type of colour or greyscale encoding used in the image (e.g., MONOCHROME2, RGB, YBR_FULL). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0028,0004).
Physical distance between the centres of adjacent pixels in the image space, specified as row and column spacing. Expressed in millimetres (mm) according to DICOM attribute (0028,0030).

A classification of the image based on the imaging modality and acquisition characteristics. It specifies the type of image produced during the scan (e.g., T1-weighted MRI, T2-weighted MRI, CT attenuation image, PET uptake image).
The digital format used to encode and store an imaging file.
The size of the file in MB.
Number of pixels in one row of the image, corresponding to the DICOM attribute Columns (0028,0011).
Number of pixels in one column of the image, corresponding to the DICOM attribute Rows (0028,0010).

The number of distinct image planes captured during acquisition. For WSI, this represents the number of focal planes (Z-stack levels). For CT, MRI, and PET, it corresponds to the number of cross-sectional slices or frames. For DX and MG, this value is typically 1 (a single 2D projection).
The number of distinct data channels stored in each pixel of the image. Channels may represent color components (e.g., RGB), grayscale intensity, or modality-specific signal dimensions.
The number of bits used to represent the stored value of each pixel channel. In DICOM, this corresponds to tag (0028,0101).
Indicates whether the image was lossy-compressed and which method was used, based on DICOM tags (0028,2110) and (0028,2114).
Indicates whether annotation data associated with the image (e.g., regions of interest, labels, markup, or segmentation overlays) are present and accessible.
Modality-specific series metadata for high-resolution digital pathology whole slide images, capturing optical scanning modes, lens magnification, illumination parameters, and focal z-stacking.
A digital image processing method which combines multiple images taken at different focal distances to create a composite image with a greater depth of field than is possible for a single image.

The objective lens magnification used for the acquisition of whole slide images, expressed as a dimensionless optical magnification factor (e.g., 10×, 20×, 40×). This refers only to the lens magnification and not the final stored image encoded by the spatial resolution attribute.
The method of optical illumination used to illuminate the specimen during scanning (e.g., brightfield, darkfield, fluorescence, phase contrast).
Nominal wavelength of the illuminator expressed in nanometres (nm).
The scanning procedure used to digitize a glass slide. This attribute does not describe the capabilities of the scanner used for digitization.
The area of the tissue region that was scanned, expressed in square millimetres (mm²).
Number of focal planes along the vertical z-axis used for multiple and extended z-stacking methods.
Distance between acquisition focal planes given in micrometers (µm).
The number of specific resolution levels of an image pyramid.

A standardised colour profile defined by the International Color Consortium (ICC) that specifies how colours in an image should be interpreted to ensure consistent colour rendering across devices (e.g. sRGB or Gray Gamma 1.8/2.2, GSDF).
An assay identifier is an identifier that identifies some assay (analysis).

A vendor-specific indicator describing the applied level or strength of lossy compression (e.g., quality level or percentage), not defined in DICOM but used in some WSI formats to express perceived compression quality.
Modality-specific series metadata for computed tomography acquisitions, capturing X-ray tube exposure parameters, spiral pitch, reconstruction convolution kernels, and slice geometry.
The peak accelerating voltage applied in an X-ray tube between the cathode and anode, corresponding to DICOM tag (0018,0060).
The value of the electrical current applied to an X-ray tube (DICOM tag (0018,1151)).
The cumulative time a subject was exposed to X-rays during image acquisition. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1150).

Ratio of the distance that the table moves during a complete revolution of the source around the gantry orbit, to the width of the total collimation over the area of active x-ray detection (DICOM tag (0018,9311)).
Specifies the type of X-ray beam–shaping filter used during image acquisition (e.g., body, head, bowtie, wedge). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1160).

An algorithm used to reconstruct imaging data. Convolution kernels can be used to filter images to smooth them and reduce noise or to enhance edges or other image features. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1210).
The physical size of the anatomical region covered in the reconstructed image, expressed in millimetres. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,9317).
The dimension between two surfaces of an imaging plane, specified in millimetres (mm). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0050).
Administration of CT contrast medium using an injector device. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1040).

The physical spacing between adjacent CT image slices along the Z-axis, representing the voxel dimension in the slice-selection direction. Expressed in millimetres (mm). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0088).

Modality-specific series metadata for magnetic resonance imaging acquisitions, capturing static magnetic field strength, radiofrequency pulse sequence timing (TR/TE), flip angle, and receive coil configurations.
The literal identifier for the pulse sequence. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0024).
A measurement of the strength of the static magnetic field (B₀) generated by an MRI system, expressed in units of Tesla (T). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0087).
The amount of time in milliseconds (ms) between successive pulse sequences applied to the same slice. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0080).
The time in milliseconds between the application of the excitation pulse and the recording of the peak echo signal. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0081).
The Larmor resonance frequency used during MR data acquisition, determined by the strength of the static magnetic field (B₀) and expressed in megahertz (MHz). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0084).

In magnetic resonance imaging, the angle by which the net magnetization vector is rotated away from the main magnetic field (B₀) by an applied radiofrequency pulse. It is expressed in degrees (°). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1314).
The time between the inversion and excitation pulses in an inversion recovery pulse sequence, expressed in milliseconds (ms). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0082).
The designated name of the radiofrequency (RF) receive coil used during MR acquisition, identifying the specific hardware component that detects the MR signal. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1250).
The physical size of the anatomical region covered in the reconstructed image, expressed in millimetres.
The dimension between two surfaces of an imaging plane, specified in millimetres (mm). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0050).
Administration of MR contrast medium using an injector device. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0010).
Modality-specific series metadata for projection digital radiography acquisitions, capturing patient orientation, X-ray tube potential, and exposure settings.
Orientation of patient relative to imaging device. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0020,0020).
The peak accelerating voltage applied in an X-ray tube between the cathode and anode, corresponding to DICOM tag (0018,0060).
The cumulative time a subject was exposed to X-rays during image acquisition. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1150).
The exposure expressed in mAs, for example calculated from Exposure Time and X-Ray Tube Current.
Modality-specific series metadata for digital mammography acquisitions, capturing dedicated breast examination projections and associated radiographic parameters.
Modality-specific series metadata for diagnostic ultrasonography acquisitions, capturing acoustic imaging parameters, anatomical focus, and real-time scanning geometry.
